name: Chien Chung-Wei (簡忠威)
fit_reason: Atmospheric urban and interior watercolor, quiet scenes, strong tonal control. Career path highly relevant: built international credibility from a Taiwan base through IWS competitions and workshops before achieving global recognition.
use_as: Primary career-path reference for building international watercolor credibility from an Asian base. Track his exhibition and competition history as a roadmap.

name: Keiko Tanabe
fit_reason: Japanese watercolor painter based in San Diego; subjects include urban scenes, travel, light, and intimate atmosphere. Has exhibited with AWS and NWS. Japan-rooted identity with international visibility — the closest structural match to GEGYjiji's potential trajectory.
use_as: Reference for Japan-origin watercolor career with international reach. Track her exhibition venues and juried show participation as a Tier 3–4 roadmap.

name: Thomas W. Schaller
fit_reason: Architectural watercolor — buildings, urban light, atmosphere, quiet structural observation. Known for large-format architectural studies with dramatic mood. Subject matter and tonal language closely aligned with GEGYjiji.
use_as: Primary reference for architectural watercolor practice and aesthetic. Study his approach to tonal values and atmospheric distance.

name: Cathy Read
fit_reason: British architectural watercolorist known for Edinburgh and UK urban scenes — buildings, street life, architectural detail. Works primarily in watercolor with occasional mixed media. Has exhibited in London and internationally, and sells through her own channels and galleries. Career stage slightly ahead of GEGYjiji but structurally comparable.
use_as: Reference for building an architectural watercolor career from a non-major-city base with direct-to-collector sales. Her gallery relationships and independent exhibition model are worth studying.

name: Lian Quan Zhen
fit_reason: Chinese-born watercolorist working in California, known for integrating Chinese ink painting sensibility with Western watercolor technique. AWS (American Watercolor Society) member. Has published instructional books on watercolor. Relevant as a model of cross-cultural practice — Chinese artistic formation applied to Western exhibition context.
use_as: Reference for cross-cultural watercolor identity — Chinese training meeting international exhibition contexts. His AWS membership and book-publishing path is one version of the Publication Track.

name: Japan Watercolor Society (日本水彩画会) exhibitors
fit_reason: Annual national exhibition (日本水彩展) held in Tokyo — Tier 3 credibility target for GEGYjiji. Exhibitors are contemporary Japanese watercolor practitioners working at the level she is building toward. Membership requires juried acceptance; the exhibition represents the Japanese institutional watercolor community.
use_as: Reference ecosystem for Japan active watercolor exhibition community. Research individual exhibitors whose subject matter (urban, architectural, atmospheric) aligns with GEGYjiji to identify peer contacts and jury taste.

name: Alvaro Castagnet
fit_reason: Urban watercolor with loose, atmospheric style; strong international exhibition record built from a non-Western, non-major-city base. AWS signature member. Career model: competed through watercolor society shows to build international reputation.
use_as: Reference for building international watercolor exhibition record through society competitions from outside the traditional Western art-world centers.

name: Huang Zeng Yuan (黄增源)
fit_reason: Contemporary Chinese watercolorist known in IWS (International Watercolour Society) circles for atmospheric, figure-and-space work. Represents the strand of the contemporary Chinese watercolor scene that works internationally through open calls and watercolor society exhibitions rather than through the Chinese gallery system.
use_as: Reference for how contemporary Chinese watercolorists participate in international open calls and IWS competitions — a route available to GEGYjiji without requiring gallery representation.

name: John Salminen
fit_reason: Architectural urban watercolor with precise draftsmanship. AWS signature member. Subject matter aligns (buildings, streets, structured observation) though his palette and scale are larger and more saturated than GEGYjiji's quiet register.
use_as: Reference for the architectural watercolor career path through American watercolor institutions. Stylistically different — useful for what NOT to reference aesthetically while tracking the institutional pathway.

name: Jean Haines
fit_reason: Prominent UK watercolor practitioner and author; books include Splash of Aquarius and Flowers in Watercolour. Style is loose, expressive, nature-focused — very different from GEGYjiji's quiet urban register. Useful only as a community reference point for the UK/international watercolor teaching world.
use_as: Community reference only — not a subject or style match. Track only for awareness of the UK watercolor teaching/publishing world. Do NOT use as a stylistic reference or aesthetic comparison.
note: Stylistically opposite to GEGYjiji. Included only for community awareness, not for aesthetic comparison.
